name_reason: Compliant: data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with battle core-table prefix data_fd2_battle_*, and the _ptr suffix reflects the primary datatype (pointer to the battle tile map). No Ghidra address residue. The slot is also overloaded by dialog code as a 0/1/2 mode flag, but the dominant/primary semantic is the tile-map pointer, which the name correctly captures; the flag-reuse is a vendor memory-overload artifact and does not warrant a name change.
purpose: Pointer to the decoded per-chapter battle tile map (from FDFIELD.DAT), with its 32-bit slot also overloaded by dialog/menu code as a small 0/1/2 rendering-mode flag.
logic_summary: Set on chapter load/save-restore from fd2_load_dat_resource(FDFIELD.DAT, chapter*3) then decrypted in place by fd2_obfuscate_battle_tile_map; freed and reset to 0 on chapter transition. As a pointer it is dereferenced for the map header (map_width/map_height = first two int16 words) and a packed array of 4-byte tile-meta records indexed ((row*map_width+col)*4+base) (sprite id = +4 ushort & 0x3FF, terrain = +6 byte & 0x1F). The dialog/menu typewriter code overloads the same slot as a 3-state mode flag: 0 = no battle map / no active dialog; 1 = full-screen intro dialog active (set before the typewriter/blink loop, reset to 0 after); >= 2 = a real tile-map pointer is loaded (in battle). Dialog code tests '1 < ptr' to detect in-battle and re-composite the battle scene behind a small dialog band instead of drawing a full-screen dialog.
datatype: uint32 (DWORD slot at .object2 0x53A51; Ghidra label is undefined/1-byte, decompiler synthesizes the 4-byte access). Holds either a byte* to the tile-map buffer or a small 0/1/2 mode flag.
element_semantics: Single 32-bit slot. Pointer mode: base address of decrypted tile-map buffer (header int16 map_width @ +0, int16 map_height @ +2, then 4-byte tile-meta records: ushort sprite_idx&0x3FF @ +4, byte terrain&0x1F @ +6). Flag mode: 0 = no map/no dialog, 1 = full-screen intro dialog, >=2 = in-battle (real pointer present).
comment_original_issue: Existing chtrans.c block was accurate but described the overload only as a '0/1 sentinel (battle map present?)', understating the actual 3-state usage (0 / 1 / >=2) the typewriter and dialog code rely on (the '1 < ptr' in-battle detection), and did not mention the free/reset-to-0 on chapter transition.
notes: Dual-use confirmed against the binary: address 0x53A51 is read as a pointer (e.g. fd2_load_chapter_battle_data @ 0x10920: *(short*)_battle_tile_map = map_width; fd2_read_tile_attribute_at_pos @ 0x12e5c) AND tested/written as a 0/1/2 flag (fd2_text_dialog_typewriter_loop @ 0x19a09 tests '1 < ptr', '== 0'; chtrans.c/misc.c/promote.c/dialog.c write =1/=0). WRITE xrefs confirm same address for both roles. is_const=false (game writes the slot via fd2_load_dat_resource result and =0/=1). Ghidra data plate at 0x53A51 was empty -> created. No logic concerns: the overload is faithful vendor behavior and is correctly preserved as a uint32 slot in the rebuild.
